title: Releasing a Co op game
author: Cold_Print6006
selftext:
I’ve been working on Lowlands Conquest for a couple of months. It’s a hack-and-slash hero game mixed with tower defense. The Steam page just went live, so I wanted to share how AI fits into my workflow.

**The setup:** I’ve used ChatGPT (Sol) and Claude (Opus / Sonnet) for pretty much everything you see in the game. Both are connected to Unity through Unity MCP and to Blender through Blender MCP. Left to themselves they tend to go low-poly. When I needed nicer assets, I had Sol generate reference images it thought would fit the game, ran those through TRELLIS 2.0 to get a 3D model, and then retopologized the result to bring the poly count down to something actually usable in-game.

**Where AI shines:** coding, and above all polish. Getting a good *feel* into the game used to take forever. Now I can iterate on it way faster.

**Where it still struggles:** animations, game balancing, and coming up with a genuinely interesting concept for a class. Those still need a human brain (and a lot of playtesting).

**One tip if you’re trying this:** if your game is first-person or otherwise lets the player get close to objects, I’d steer clear of AI-generated 3D models for now, whether from TRELLIS or Tripo. They’re still murky up close and nowhere near sharp. They work much better at a distance.

I’d love feedback on the page or the game, and I’m happy to answer questions about any part of the pipeline.
